title: Three lenses on the Old Quarter
tagline: From belief and family homes to the rhythm of the market
intro:
Among Hà Nội's busy streets, have you ever wondered what has shaped the Old Quarter's identity over the centuries?

The city's memories live in more than grand monuments. Sometimes they are held in a temple roof, a modest house or a crowded market. On this journey, Ngõ Kể explores three perspectives on Hà Nội's Old Quarter.

We begin at Bạch Mã Temple with a legend linked to the citadel of Thăng Long, continue to the heritage house at 87 Mã Mây to discover everyday life through its architecture, and finish at Đồng Xuân Market, a trading centre that has witnessed many changes.

Each place tells a story. Together, they offer a view of the city's culture, people and urban history. These are three separate places, not three stops within a single alley, and this experience does not provide walking directions.

chapters.title: The white horse and Thăng Long's eastern guardian
chapters.hook: On Hàng Buồm Street stands a temple called Bạch Mã, meaning white horse. How did a horse become part of a story about building the citadel of Thăng Long?
chapters.story:
Bạch Mã Temple is a historic place of worship on Hàng Buồm Street, dedicated to Long Đỗ, a deity associated with protecting the land of Thăng Long. The temple is known as the eastern guardian in the traditional system of Thăng Long's four guardian temples.

According to legend, King Lý Thái Tổ repeatedly encountered difficulties while building the citadel. After prayers were offered to the deity, a white horse appeared and left hoofprints. The king ordered the walls to follow those tracks, and the work was completed.

The white horse story is a folk legend. It expresses a belief in divine protection; it is not a historically proven account of construction. Through repeated repairs, Bạch Mã Temple has remained a place of worship connected with Hà Nội's long memory.
chapters.observation: In the supplied photograph, look for the tiled roof and its decorative details, the Chinese-character sign above the main entrance, and the wooden doors and front columns. The image does not establish the exact age of these features. This is a place of worship: remain quiet, respect religious activities, and take photographs only where permitted.

chapters.title: One house, many generations
chapters.hook: Have you ever wondered how people once lived in the Old Quarter's houses with their narrow street frontages?
chapters.story:
The heritage house at 87 Mã Mây preserves features of traditional housing in Hà Nội's Old Quarter. Its frontage is narrow, but the plot extends deep behind the street. The front rooms were used for trade, with family living spaces further inside. Small courtyards between the buildings bring in light and allow air to circulate.

According to the Department of Cultural Heritage, the owner before 1945 traded in rice. Later, the house was used as a home and a place to sell traditional herbal medicine. At one stage, several families lived here together.

In 1999, the building was restored through a conservation partnership between Hà Nội and Toulouse in France. In 2004, the house was listed as a national monument. It offers visitors a way to understand life in the Old Quarter. Sources disagree about its original construction date, so this account does not give an exact year.
chapters.observation: In the supplied photograph, notice the Heritage House sign, the central wooden doors, the wooden balustrade above, the tiled roof and the wall colour. If entry is permitted, you can also look at the sequence of rooms and courtyards. Enter or photograph the interior only when allowed; check visiting arrangements at the time of your visit.

chapters.title: Đồng Xuân: more than a century of change
chapters.hook: The supplied 2026 photograph shows a thirtieth-anniversary banner on Đồng Xuân Market's facade. But the market's history stretches back much further than thirty years.
chapters.story:
Đồng Xuân Market is a longstanding trading centre connected with the growth of Hà Nội's Old Quarter. Archival material records steel-framed market halls with metal roofs here in 1890. Increasing trade led to further expansion.

In 1917, plans were made for an additional hall and a facade with five large arches. The dates 1996–2026 on the banner in the supplied photograph refer to thirty years since Đồng Xuân Corporation was established in 1996, not the age of the market itself.

After many phases of change, Đồng Xuân remains an important part of Hà Nội's commercial history. This account does not claim that today's entire facade survives unchanged from 1890.
chapters.observation: In the photograph, look at the facade, the repeated openings and decorative features, the 2026 anniversary banner, and the trading activity in front. The banner belongs to the time of the photograph; it is not a permanent feature or a guarantee of what is displayed today.

chapters.title: The fire of 1994
chapters.hook: It can be hard to imagine that the busy market shown in these photographs once suffered a devastating fire.
chapters.story:
The supplied interior photograph shows layers of stalls and walkways beneath the market's high roof. Yet this place has also experienced a major disaster.

In 1994, a fire burned through almost all the market's stalls, seriously disrupting trading. In 1995, Đồng Xuân Market was rebuilt as a three-storey complex so that buying and selling could continue.

The story of the market is therefore about more than architecture. It is also about the traders whose working lives have been connected with this place through periods of change.
chapters.observation: Look at the high roof, the arrangement of floors and stalls, and the central water feature visible in the supplied photograph. The sources checked do not establish when that water feature was built. Do not assume it dates from the French colonial period.

chapters.title: Everyday life beside the market
chapters.hook: Beyond the halls is another view of Đồng Xuân: small food stalls, passing people and the everyday rhythm of the surrounding streets.
chapters.story:
Đồng Xuân is more than a large market building. Commercial life also takes place on the streets around it. From the late nineteenth century, the market brought together goods from within the country and from abroad. Connections with trading streets and transport links helped it become an important commercial centre.

Goods, vehicles and ways of trading have changed over time. Around the market, shops and streetside food businesses remain part of everyday life.

These ordinary scenes remind us that Hà Nội's history is not held only in old buildings. It also continues through the lives of people today. The supplied photograph records one moment, rather than proving the current operation or history of every business shown.
chapters.observation: Notice the side of the market building, the streetside food stalls, the traffic and trading activity, and the connection between the large market and smaller businesses. Do not describe a particular stall as longstanding or family-run without evidence for that business.

transitions: Leaving the story of deities and the citadel, we turn to a different perspective on Hà Nội. Our next place is a house on Mã Mây Street, where everyday life in the Old Quarter can be explored through architecture. This is a narrative transition, not walking directions.

From the house on Mã Mây Street, the journey continues to a much larger space. If 87 Mã Mây tells a story of families and generations of residents, Đồng Xuân Market introduces trading, upheaval and the city's commercial rhythm. This is a narrative transition, not walking directions.
closing:
Our journey began at Bạch Mã Temple, with a legend linked to the building of Thăng Long. At the heritage house at 87 Mã Mây, we explored how people organised home and work in the Old Quarter. At Đồng Xuân Market, we encountered trading across generations, through upheaval and change.

Three places offer three perspectives: belief, family life and commerce. This is what Ngõ Kể hopes to share: not only where a place is, but the cultural stories behind it. Walk through a street, discover layers of Hà Nội's memory. Visiting arrangements, routes and access still need to be checked locally.
summaries: Long Đỗ, the white horse legend and Thăng Long's eastern guardian.
Trade, courtyards and family life in a traditional Old Quarter house.
Three chapters at one market: change, the 1994 fire and surrounding street life.
captions: Bạch Mã: a place of worship; the white horse account is a legend.
87 Mã Mây: narrow frontage, deep rooms and courtyards for light and air.
Đồng Xuân: three narrative chapters at one real place, not three GPS stops.

qa.question: Which deity is worshipped at Bạch Mã Temple?
qa.answer: The temple is dedicated to Long Đỗ, a deity associated in folk belief with protecting the land of Thăng Long.

qa.question: Why is the temple called Bạch Mã?
qa.answer: According to legend, a white horse appeared and left hoofprints that helped King Lý Thái Tổ build the citadel. This is a religious folk story, not an event proven by historical records.

qa.question: Which of Thăng Long's four guardians is Bạch Mã Temple?
qa.answer: Bạch Mã Temple is the eastern guardian, one of the four temples traditionally believed to protect the citadel of Thăng Long.

qa.question: Why does 87 Mã Mây have a narrow frontage and a deep layout?
qa.answer: This is a common feature of the Old Quarter's tube houses. Their spaces are arranged in layers combining trade, family life and courtyards for daylight and ventilation.

qa.question: What was sold in this house in the past?
qa.answer: According to the Department of Cultural Heritage, the owner before 1945 traded in rice. Later, the house was used as a home and for selling traditional herbal medicine.

qa.question: When was the heritage house at 87 Mã Mây restored?
qa.answer: In 1999, through a conservation partnership between Hà Nội and Toulouse in France.

qa.question: In exactly which year was the house originally built?
qa.answer: The available sources disagree about its original construction date. Ngõ Kể therefore does not give an exact year.
aliases: when was the house first built

qa.question: How far back does Đồng Xuân Market's history go?
qa.answer: Archival material records steel-framed market halls with metal roofs here in 1890. The market's history is linked with the development of trade in Hà Nội.

qa.question: Why does the banner say thirty years?
qa.answer: The dates 1996–2026 mark thirty years since Đồng Xuân Corporation was established. They do not refer to the age of the market. The banner is shown in the supplied 2026 photograph.

qa.question: Has today's market facade remained unchanged since 1890?
qa.answer: There is no basis for that claim. Đồng Xuân Market has undergone several phases of building, expansion and renovation.

qa.question: In which year did the major Đồng Xuân Market fire occur?
qa.answer: A major fire occurred in 1994, burning through almost all the market's stalls.

qa.question: When was the market rebuilt after the fire?
qa.answer: In 1995, Đồng Xuân Market was rebuilt as a three-storey complex.

qa.question: Does the water feature inside the market date from the French colonial period?
qa.answer: The reliable sources checked do not establish when that water feature was built. Ngõ Kể does not draw a conclusion about its age.

qa.question: Why did Đồng Xuân become an important trading centre?
qa.answer: Its connections with trading streets and transport links, together with the range of goods brought from different regions, helped it develop as a commercial centre.

qa.question: What kinds of goods were traded at Đồng Xuân in the past?
qa.answer: Historical accounts describe a variety of goods, including local products, textiles and imports.

qa.question: Are all the food stalls around the market longstanding businesses?
qa.answer: That cannot be concluded. Food businesses operate around the market, but each stall's age and history must be verified separately.
